text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- Swiss President Arnold Koller flew to Prague for an official visit with Czech President Vaclav Havel and other leaders. Koller discussed cross border corruption and European integration.
- The number of people seeking asylum in Switzerland grew in the first five months of the year by 21.7 percent to 8,286, compared to the same period in 1996.
- Berna AG, a division of the Saurer Group, acquired U.S. firm Multi-Arc in Rockaway for $29 million.
- Lonza Biologics, a subsidiary of Alusuisse-Lonza, plans to cooperate with U.S. pharma group Ely Lilly to develop and manufacture an unspecified therapeutic protein.

- The New York Times reported yesterday that at least $40 million in funds owned most likely by Holocaust victims are resting unclaimed in Swiss banks. The Swiss Bankers Association denied the report, saying the numbers were a "misunderstanding". - Farmers in Swiss mountain regions will share a total of 1.3 billion Swiss francs in government subsidies over the next three years.
- The European Commission approved the merger of Clariant with Germany's special chemicals firm Hoechst.
